title: The Dome of the Rock
hook: a golden dome in Jerusalem over the rock linked with the night journey

segments.voice: Yesterday: Damascus, one ruling house from the Atlantic to the Indus. Your line was from spain to sindh.

Inside, the light drops. You come in from the bright stone plaza, and your eyes adjust. Columns of marble. Gold mosaic catching what light there is. And in the middle, behind a railing, not a floor at all but a great bare outcrop of rock, rough and uneven, the hill itself coming up through the building. Everything else was built around it. Above it, the dome. This is Jerusalem, on the high plaza Muslims call al-Haram al-Sharif, the Noble Sanctuary. Today: the Dome of the Rock.

Start with the journey. The Qur'an opens one surah with it: "Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship." The Inviolable Place is the Kaaba in Mecca. The Far Distant Place, al-Masjid al-Aqsa, is understood in Islamic tradition as Jerusalem. The hadith collections tell how, from there, the Prophet ﷺ was taken up through the heavens, and tradition links that ascent with this rock. The rock is holy in Jewish tradition too, on the hill where the Temple stood. Now the building. Tradition says the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik had it raised over the rock. Its plan is an octagon, with rings of columns, so pilgrims can walk around the rock beneath the dome. One distinction: the Dome of the Rock is not the mosque. It's a shrine. The mosque for congregational prayer, al-Aqsa Mosque, stands at the southern end of the same plaza. Look up inside and a long band of Arabic runs around the walls in gold mosaic: verses of the Qur'an, including verses about Jesus son of Mary, whom the Qur'an honors as a messenger. Outside, the walls blaze with blue and white tiles, added in a later age, so the building has been dressed by more than one generation. A city holy to many, a journey by night, and over the spot, a dome over the rock.
screen: then, large: `A DOME OVER THE ROCK.`

segments.voice: If you can, look at a close photo of the outer tiles and follow one line of the pattern until it turns and meets itself, noticing the writing woven into the design. Then close your eyes and picture the rock inside, untouched, with the whole building shaped around it. If you pray, you can recite the opening of Surah al-Isra: glorified be He who carried His servant by night.
Sakhrah, the rock itself: the bare stone at the center of the shrine, linked in tradition with the Prophet's night journey and holy in Jewish tradition too. Today's word.
Your line: a dome over the rock. Built around it, not over it. That's day nine hundred four.

howItsDone: Muslims visiting Jerusalem pray at al-Aqsa Mosque and visit the Dome of the Rock on the same plaza, and the night journey is remembered on the night Muslims call al-Isra wal-Mi'raj.
